UnitStatement: RulePackManagerPanel.tsx is the desktop Rule-Pack Manager (PRD §14.5 / §14.1): list/create/open/save/delete packs against the local-only store, with validation findings and checksum generation/stamping.
The rule-pack manager operates against a local-only store; packs are project-scoped and nothing is stored until the user saves.

Rule-pack authoring was built in slices: slice 1 raw canonical JSON; slice 2 structured AST expression composer; slice 3 table-backed nodes; slice 4 variable-declarations editor; slice 5 check-definitions editor.
The full grammar v1.0.0 node set (DEC-022) is built through form/tree controls rather than hand-written JSON.
The raw document JSON remains the canonical/fallback surface for remaining metadata members: diagnostics, classification, checksums, provenance, professional_boundary, open_decisions.
DEC-037 permits a labeled read-only one-way AST-to-text preview, but provides no writable expression text syntax or parser.
NO_DRAFT_REASON: no draft rule-pack document exists; create a new draft or open a stored pack first.
NO_PROJECT_REASON: local rule packs are project-scoped; create or open a local project first.
BUSY_REASON: a rule-pack backend request is in progress; wait for it to finish before editing or running another action.
RulePackR3JourneyEvent enumerates rule-pack journey events: rule_pack_draft_created, rule_pack_validate_requested, rule_pack_checksum_requested, rule_pack_save_requested.
An in-request busy guard (inFlight) disables the draft editors and all actions while a backend command is awaiting, so an async response cannot clobber a mid-request edit.
When the active project changes, the previously-listed packs are cleared (they belong to the old project), but the session draft is intentionally preserved until saved.

Backend (Tauri) commands can reject in desktop mode; browser preview short-circuits to an explicit unavailable route, while a desktop backend error is surfaced honestly rather than as a silent unhandled rejection.
parseDraft validates that the draft text is a JSON object (not array/null/primitive), reporting RULE-PACK-DRAFT-JSON-INVALID on failure.
handleNewDraft creates a new private draft in memory with privacy_class=private_user_data and redistribution_status=private_only; nothing is stored until saved.
handleRefreshList lists local rule packs for the project; browser preview returns route unavailable_browser_preview.
handleValidate validates the draft document and reports blocking_findings, checksum match_status, and grammar_supported.
handleComputeChecksum computes the rule-pack checksum, stamps it into the draft document, and reports the basis and payload_excludes.
handleSave requires a project; it saves the draft to the local store, reporting rule_pack_id and storage_mode, then refreshes the list.
handleOpen loads a stored rule pack from the local store into the draft and shows its validation.
handleDelete deletes a stored rule pack from the local store and refreshes the list.
Structured editors (composer, declarations, check-definitions) re-serialize the edited document back into the canonical draft text, the single source of truth the validate/checksum/save flow reads.

The rule-pack document JSON is the native canonical form; the editors author required-input/value-slot declarations, the formula expression AST (declarative-AST per DEC-022 including table-backed nodes), and acceptability check definitions.
Boundary note: private rule packs stay in local project storage only and are never committed, transmitted, or bundled into public artifacts.
Boundary note: rule-check output is a software computation over user-supplied data, never a code-compliance, certification, sealing, approval, or professional acceptance claim.
collectFindings aggregates document_findings, lifecycle_findings, and per-formula findings into a single validation findings list.
RunAuditPanel renders run audit references (model-state, analysis-run, status, hash evidence, input manifest, reproducibility TBDs, immutability, boundary) from an AnalysisRunEnvelope.
Hash evidence is summarized as result row count, result value hash count, and hash payload scopes.
Empty state: run mechanics preview to generate immutable model-state and analysis-run audit references for the local fixture.
Boundary note: run audit evidence is local technical-preview context, not a release or professional acceptance record.
immutabilitySummary describes the run immutability policy: read-only run record, changes require a new run, and hash changes invalidate external acceptance.
boundarySummary asserts the professional boundary requires human review and makes no compliance, certification, sealing, authentication, or approval claim.

SecretPrivateReference describes a metadata-only reference whose record_kind is one of private_material_library, private_component_library, private_rule_pack, private_path_reference, or secret_field_reference.

Every SecretPrivateReference carries contains_payload=false, secret_material_present=false, concrete_path_present=false, cloud_or_network_reference=false, external_secret_manager_reference=false, direct_sql_access=false, storage_bypass_requested=false.
GuardDecision records a release-context disposition: action is block_release or include_metadata_only, with metadata_only=true.
SecretPrivateLibraryPanel reviews secret and private-library references as metadata-only and offers a local JSON download of the boundary-review packet.
buildSecretPrivateLibraryPacket assembles the secret_private_library_boundary_review document (DEL-12-04, PKG-12) with guard decisions for public_report, public_fixture, and local_private contexts.
Guard policy: public_report references are included metadata-only, public_fixture references are blocked from release, and local_private references are included metadata-only.
The packet summary asserts private_payload_included=false, protected_content_included=false, and release_or_professional_claim=false.

no_bypass_controls require adapters to preserve redaction, deny plugins by default, and forbid direct SQL, raw SQLite handles, storage bypass, network, telemetry, and private/protected payload copying.

runtime_deferrals mark exact_secret_provider, encrypted_storage_default, storage_roots, permission_grant_persistence, public_api_transport, and external_secret_manager_behavior as TBD; cloud_or_network_behavior is not_authorized_in_preview.
secretPrivateReferences seeds four invented preview references: a private material library, a private rule pack, a private library-root path, and an import credential placeholder.
guardDecisions maps each reference to a release decision per context, generating decision IDs of form SPL-GRD-NNNN-<context>.

Boundary note: secret/private-library review records metadata-only references and does not store credential values, read private libraries, choose a secret provider, finalize encryption/key management, or create security, professional, certification, sealing, authentication, approval, or code-compliance reliance.
ThreatReviewRow describes a threat with threat_id, surface, initial_risk (High or Medium/High), and required_posture.
SecurityThreatModelPanel renders the threat model review and offers a local JSON download of the threat packet.

buildSecurityThreatModelPacket assembles the security_threat_model_review document (DEL-12-05, PKG-12, SOW-040, OBJ-010) from threat inventory, trust boundaries, asset classes, export workflows, and open decisions.
The threat packet summary reports local_first=true, telemetry_default_off=true, and release_or_professional_claim=false.

assetClasses enumerates ten protected asset classes including project/model data, rule packs, material/component libraries, reports, diagnostics, plugin manifests, import/export data, SCA-004 export packages, secrets, and build artifacts.

trustBoundaries enumerates ten trust boundaries including local filesystem, public repository, report export/share, target export packages, external CAEPIPE/harness execution, telemetry, plugins, rule evaluator, and the build/release supply chain.

exportWorkflows enumerates six export workflows: common export packages, CAEPIPE MBF/external harness, stress-neutral CSV/JSON, conservative PCF subset, GLB/GLTF review geometry, and the export adapter SDK.

threatInventory lists nineteen threats (STM-001..STM-019) each pairing a surface with a required posture, e.g. local_storage (private path exclusion), telemetry (disabled by default), plugins (deny by default no bypass).

openDecisions lists unresolved decisions; storage_substrate is SCA-003 local SQLite-backed store selected, while storage roots, schema/DB migration, encryption, secret storage, plugin permission model, and telemetry schema remain TBD.
professionalBoundary asserts human_review_required=true and that the software makes no compliance, security-certification, certification, sealing, approval, or authentication claim.

Boundary note: threat model review is local preview evidence only; it does not prove security sufficiency, authorize telemetry, certify release readiness, or create professional/code-compliance reliance.
safeFileToken normalizes a string into a filesystem-safe lowercase token by replacing non-alphanumerics with hyphens.
SolvePanel is the execution panel: it shows mechanics/rule-check/professional-acceptance status, a readiness summary, a solve-job audit packet, and run/cancel controls.
ReadinessItem has a tone of ok, info, warning, or blocking for the mechanics, rule, diagnostics, and professional readiness rows.
readinessSummary builds four readiness rows summarizing computed result rows, rule-check completeness, diagnostic warning/blocking counts, and professional-boundary status.
ruleReadiness reports that when rule inputs are incomplete/missing/not_performed, mechanics results remain reviewable only.
professionalReadiness reports that human review is required and no professional acceptance record exists when status is not_provided.
buildSolveJobPacket assembles the solve_job_audit document (DEL-07-07/DEL-14-02/DEL-04-06) summarizing job state, events, result rows, progress contract, cancellation, and result binding.
The progress_contract records whether percentages are synthesized and whether a backend percent stream is available, plus the latest event state.

Cancellation is cooperative: with a tauri_backend_job seam the scope is cooperative_checkpoints_not_preemptive, otherwise it is a UI request record only; it never mutates the solver process directly and never claims cancellation success.
The Run mechanics preview control is disabled while running; the Cancel preview control is disabled when nothing is running.
boundarySummary asserts private payload=false, protected content=false, release/professional claim=false, and human review required.
STRESS_NEUTRAL_EXPORT_VERSION is 0.1.0; the browser preview does not emit a canonical package hash (HASH_STATUS_TBD) and schema is shape-aligned not runtime JSON-schema validated.
The stress-neutral CSV columns are: result_id, canonical_ref, row_kind, result_family, load_case_ref, station_ref, component_ref, value, unit, dimension, correlation_status.
A StressNeutralRow carries value, unit, dimension, and a correlation_status of either canonical_id_map or unit_or_dimension_blocking_review_required.
StressNeutralUnitPreservationWitness records source and target quantities with export_unit_policy=preserve_source_result_unit_and_dimension and conversion_performed=false.
StressNeutralExportPanel assembles a stress-neutral CSV/JSON export package and offers JSON and CSV downloads when a result and analysis run are present.

buildStressNeutralExportPacket assembles the stress_neutral_csv_json_package (DEL-17-06, PKG-17) with result rows, unit witnesses, stable ID map, loss report, manifest, validation report, and diagnostics.

The export profile ops.stress_neutral.v1 requires unit and dimension per row, a canonical ref per row plus a stable ID map, a mandatory loss report, and diagnostic-export-only comparison semantics (no pass/fail).
The loss report records exported rows, comparison-semantics TBD (consumers must not infer acceptance/compliance), and redacted private rule payload.

The validation report runs checks for CSV/JSON row sync, canonical ref per row, unit and dimension per row, unit-preservation witness per row, witness/row match, stable-id-map per row, and loss-report presence.
stressNeutralRow assigns correlation_status canonical_id_map only when unit and a non-TBD dimension are present, else unit_or_dimension_blocking_review_required.
witnessMatchesRow verifies a unit-preservation witness matches its row on source/target refs, value, unit, dimension, and conversion_performed=false.
resultFamily classifies a result as displacement, reaction, force, moment, stress, or ratio from its kind and id.
resultDimension maps families to dimensions: displacement->length, reaction/force->force, moment->moment, stress->stress, ratio->dimensionless, rotation->angle, else TBD.

The stress-neutral professional boundary supports review, regression comparison input, and downstream tooling, but not release readiness, external target compatibility, solver validation, code compliance, certification, sealing, approval, or professional reliance.
previewProvenance marks source as the OpenPipeStress desktop technical preview, license PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0, redistribution_status invented_non_engineering_example, review_status pending.
Boundary note: stress-neutral export is a local technical-preview review package only, not a vendor format, solver input deck, solver validation, code compliance, or professional reliance record.

A TelemetryAttempt records an attempted event with field classes and a decision whose action is drop_disabled or reject_forbidden_surface, with payload_constructed=false and network_behavior_initialized=false.
TelemetryBoundaryPanel reviews the telemetry boundary and offers a local JSON download of the telemetry packet.

buildTelemetryBoundaryPacket assembles the telemetry_boundary_review document (DEL-12-03, PKG-12, SOW-037, OBJ-010) reporting config resolution, the metadata-only guard, event attempts, and runtime initialization state.
All telemetry events are blocked: allowed_event_count=0, payload_constructed=false, network_transport_initialized=false; config resolves disabled by default.
The metadata-only guard runs before payload construction and does not authorize runtime telemetry; product config schema is TBD.
runtime_initialization confirms no network transport, endpoint, vendor, upload queue/job, telemetry persistence, external service client, or background job is initialized.

Forbidden telemetry payload classes include private project models, code-specific rule data, private rule packs, private libraries, generated reports/exports, model hashes, local file paths, secrets, protected standards content, and professional/code-compliance claims.
telemetryEventAttempts seeds four events; app_started, project_opened, and solve_requested are dropped (disabled), and report_export_attempted is rejected as a forbidden surface.
disabledAttempt marks operational-metadata events with action drop_disabled and reason telemetry_disabled_no_opt_in_or_allowlist.

Boundary note: telemetry remains default-off and no-op in this preview; the review records policy and guard state only and does not authorize collection, transport, endpoint, vendor, support-bundle upload, security certification, or professional/code-compliance reliance.

MANUAL_SECTIONS lists ten validation-manual sections including product scope, solver theory, unit/schema verification, element verification, stress recovery, nonlinear support, rule-pack evaluator, GUI workflow, report reproducibility, and known limitations.

EVIDENCE_AREAS lists eight evidence areas including mechanics benchmarks, stress-recovery benchmarks, nonlinear support regression, GUI workflow validation, report protected-content lint, release quality, evidence bundles, and professional boundary.

Release profiles are skeleton, python, security, cargo, and all; required release paths include BUILD_AND_RELEASE.md, RELEASE_QUALITY_GATES.md, VALIDATION_STRATEGY.md, IP_AND_DATA_BOUNDARY.md, and PROFESSIONAL_BOUNDARY.md.
Open validation decisions include benchmark tolerance policy, public benchmark source acceptance, release label policy, GUI validation evidence requirements, and validation evidence bundle storage.
Release gate families are solver, rule_engine, gui, report_template, and mixed.
ValidationEvidencePanel renders the validation/release evidence review and offers a local JSON download.

buildValidationEvidencePacket assembles the validation_release_evidence_review document referencing the validation strategy, validation manual, release quality gates, build/release docs, and the release-readiness tool.
The validation manual separates mechanics validation, rule evaluation, and professional reliance; evidence states are PLANNED, DRAFT_EVIDENCE, MAINTAINER_REVIEWED, BLOCKED, and TBD.
The release-readiness tool (tools/release/check_release_readiness.py) runs dry-run by default, requires no external services, and is not executed by the browser panel.
Release quality gates record release_publication_authorized=false, that no waiver can authorize protected/private exposure, and that gates are software-quality evidence only.

Boundary note: validation evidence is local technical-preview review context only; it organizes software-quality evidence and unresolved decisions but does not authorize release, certify engineering work, or make code-compliance claims.
PipeViewport Props include model, optional onQueueIntent, onSelect, queuedIntents, optional result, and selection.
ViewportCommandType is one of create_node, connect_pipe_run, or insert_component_symbol.
NodeDraft captures id, label, coordinateUnit, and x/y/z coordinate strings for an explicit node.
PipeDraft captures id, label, from/to nodes, material, lengthUnit, outside diameter, wall thickness, a y-reference vector, and provenance for an explicit straight pipe.
DeformationOverlay state is one of not_started, available, blocked, or unavailable, with a summary, boundary note, and node positions map.
PipeViewport is the 3D centerline viewport: it renders nodes, pipe segments, supports, components, and an optional deformation overlay, and authors explicit node/pipe create intents.
On mount the viewport loads the unit catalog, falling back to an unavailable_browser_preview route on error.
The viewport falls back to a non-WebGL message when WebGL is unavailable, while still loading model data in the tree.
The Three.js scene builds a perspective camera, lights, grid, and meshes for pipe segments, deformed pipes, deformation markers, node markers, supports, and components.
Editor gestures queue EditorOperationIntent records (create_node, connect_pipe_run, insert_component_symbol) rather than mutating persisted project data.
chooseViewportTarget, when a pipe endpoint pick is armed and a node is targeted, assigns the node to the from/to endpoint and advances the pick mode, then selects the target.
captureNodeDraftFromViewport projects a viewport pointer event to a 3D point and seeds a node draft from it.
Empty-intent state: editor gestures create pending service-validation intents; they do not mutate persisted project data directly.
Queued intents are marked pending_service_validation, requiring unit_aware_domain_validation, and do not mutate the persisted project payload.
isNodeDraftValid requires a non-empty id and label, a valid (non-TBD) coordinate unit, and finite x/y/z values.
isPipeDraftValid requires id, label, distinct from/to nodes, material, a valid length unit, provenance, positive OD and wall, and a non-zero finite y-reference vector.
validUnitSymbol treats a unit symbol as valid only when it is non-empty and not TBD.
unitOptions sources length-unit options from accepted, dimension-matching entries of the loaded DEC-018 unit catalog, prepending the current fallback symbol.
nextViewportNodeId allocates the next unused node id of form node:V-NNN, reserving existing nodes and queued create-node intents.
raycastDraftPoint raycasts a pointer against the ground plane (y=0) to produce a draft 3D point, returning null when there is no finite intersection.
The viewport unit-catalog status reports the loaded DEC-018 unit catalog entry count, or that browser preview uses model metadata for length units.
